paper_metadata.title: The effect of Nb element on microstructure and properties of CoCuFeMnNbxNi high-entropy alloys

evidence.quote: This study modifies the microstructure and properties of CoCuFeMnNi HEAs by varying the Nb content.

For the CoCuFeMnNi alloy, which served as the matrix, the patterns revealed a single FCC diffraction peak (JCPDS#89 – 4185).

SAED analysis, shown in Fig. 4 (b and c), confirms that both regions possessed FCC structures. The diffraction spots obtained along the [001] crystallographic axis are denoted as FCC phase and Cu-rich FCC phase, respectively.
As shown in Fig. 3 (b), the Nb0.25 alloy exhibited white second-phase particles, which were identified as Nb-rich Laves phases through EDS point analysis combined with XRD data.
The diffraction patterns for Regions I and II, obtained along the [001] crystallographic axis, confirm them as FCC phase and Cu-rich FCC phase, respectively.
The diffraction patterns for Regions I and II, obtained along the [001] crystallographic axis, confirm them as FCC phase and Cu-rich FCC phase, respectively.
In contrast, the diffraction patterns for Region III, obtained along the [122] and [011] crystallographic axes, identify it as the Laves phase with an HCP structure, consistent with the XRD results.
